newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada rejects PolyGram film bid - paper.
newsitem.headline: Canada rejects PolyGram film bid - paper.

text.p: The Financial Post reported on Thursday that the Canadian government had rejected a request by PolyGram NV to be able to distribute movies freely in Canada.
"Sources said PolyGram's request to be allowed to distribute movies freely in Canada has been turned down. An official ruling has not been issued," the newspaper reported.

PolyGram, 75 percent owned by Philips Electronics NV, had sought exemption from strict rules intended to protect Canadian film distributors and producers, promising in return to invest heavily in the Canadian film industry.

PolyGram contended that Canada's cultural restrictions had failed to foster a strong Canadian film industry, and that the opposition Bloc Quebecois had urged the Liberal government to block PolyGram from distributing independent movies in Canada.
